hints.title: Simulation by Arrival and Execution Duration
hints.text: Sort tasks by arrival time while preserving original indices, and manage currently available tasks.

hints.title: Available Tasks by Shortest Duration
hints.text: Maintain ready tasks ordered primarily by processing time and secondarily by original index.

hints.title: Time Advancement Jump
hints.text: If no tasks are currently ready, advance the current clock directly to the next arrival time.

hints.title: Full Implementation
hints.text:
```python
import heapq

class Solution:
    def getOrder(self, tasks: list[list[int]]) -> list[int]:
        indexed = sorted([(t[0], t[1], i) for i, t in enumerate(tasks)])
        pq = []
        ans = []
        curr_time = 0
        idx = 0
        n = len(tasks)

        while idx < n or pq:
            if not pq and curr_time < indexed[idx][0]:
                curr_time = indexed[idx][0]

            while idx < n and indexed[idx][0] <= curr_time:
                heapq.heappush(pq, (indexed[idx][1], indexed[idx][2]))
                idx += 1

            duration, orig_idx = heapq.heappop(pq)
            curr_time += duration
            ans.append(orig_idx)

        return ans
```

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Scanning all remaining tasks to pick the shortest at each step takes O(n^2) quadratic time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Dual sorting and priority queue selection executes task scheduling in O(n log n) total time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate advances simulation time forward to next task arrival when processor is idle.
